plugins.name: AI command
plugins.description: Say what you want in plain words — “find the 10 biggest files changed this week”, “undo my last commit but keep the changes” — and Claude types the matching shell command at your prompt for you to check and run.

plugins.name: AI explain
plugins.description: Stuck on a wall of red? One command sends what is on screen, plus the command you ran and its exit code, to Claude and opens a scrollable explanation of what went wrong and how to fix it.

plugins.name: AI fix
plugins.description: Your last command failed? Run ``fix`` and Claude reads the error on screen and types a corrected command at your prompt — typos, wrong flags, missing sudo, the lot.

plugins.name: Smart tab titles
plugins.description: Tabs name themselves: while a command runs the tab shows what it is with an icon (🐍 python, 🦀 cargo, 🐳 docker, ⎈ kubectl, 🌐 ssh host…), and at the prompt it shows the Git repository and branch you are in.

plugins.name: Busy orbit
plugins.description: While a command runs for more than a few seconds, a glowing comet orbits the border of its window, so you can see at a glance that something is still working.

plugins.name: Command timer
plugins.description: Kick off a slow build and walk away: when a long command finishes in a window you are not looking at, a desktop notification tells you what finished, whether it worked and how long it took.

plugins.name: Color picker
plugins.description: A true color picker inside your terminal: steer hue, saturation and lightness with the keyboard, see a big live swatch with complementary and analogous harmonies, and copy the result as hex, rgb() or hsl().

plugins.name: Command stats
plugins.description: Your shell, quantified: every command is logged locally, and a full screen dashboard shows your most used tools, failure rates, time sunk into builds, your busiest hours and the slowest commands of the week.

plugins.name: Daylight themes
plugins.description: Your terminal follows the sun: colors drift continuously from deep night blue through dawn rose and crisp daylight to dusk amber as the hours pass.

plugins.name: Emoji picker
plugins.description: A fast, searchable emoji grid: type to filter by name across every emoji Unicode knows, move with the arrow keys and press Enter to type the emoji into your terminal. Recently used emoji come first.

plugins.name: Fail glitch
plugins.description: When a command fails, the screen glitches: RGB split, torn scanlines and a red flash, scaled by how bad the failure was.

plugins.name: File peek
plugins.description: Browse the current directory in a split overlay with a live, syntax-highlighted preview of whatever is under the cursor. Press Enter on a file to drop its path, shell-quoted, at your prompt.

plugins.name: Git dashboard
plugins.description: Everything about the repository you are in on one screen: branch and upstream drift, staged / changed / untracked files with diff stats, stashes, and a colored commit graph.

plugins.name: Git mood light
plugins.description: An ambient light that shows the state of the repository you are in: calm green when clean, amber with changes, red during merge conflicts, violet when ahead of the remote, blue on a detached HEAD.

plugins.name: Load heatwave
plugins.description: Feel your machine working: when CPU load climbs, heat shimmer rises from the bottom of the terminal and the glow turns from orange to angry red.

plugins.name: Pomodoro aura
plugins.description: A focus timer you can feel: a glowing progress bar across the top of kitty, and an aura that warms from cool teal to amber as the focus session runs out. Breaks breathe in soft green.

plugins.name: Prod guard
plugins.description: Never mistake production for staging again: when a command touches production, that window turns blood red and kitty draws hazard stripes around it until the command ends.

plugins.name: Reopen closed
plugins.description: Ctrl+Shift+T for your terminal: closed a shell by accident? Bring it back in the same directory with the same title, or pick from the last twenty closed shells.

plugins.name: Screen watcher
plugins.description: Tell kitty what you are waiting for (“compiled successfully”, “ERROR”, a request ID…) and go do something else: when it appears in the watched window you get a notification, a flash of light and a 🔔 in the tab title.

plugins.name: Smart scroll
plugins.description: Scroll kitty history normally and forward the same keys to alternate-screen applications.

plugins.name: Snake
plugins.description: The classic, rendered in true color inside a kitty overlay: a gradient snake that speeds up as it grows, glowing food, wrap-free walls and a high score that survives restarts. For compile breaks.

plugins.name: SSH host themes
plugins.description: Every server gets its own color: when you ssh somewhere, that window takes on a tint, cursor and border color derived from the host name, so the same host always looks the same and different hosts never look alike.

plugins.name: Streak fireworks
plugins.description: Gamifies your shell: every successful command builds a streak, and streak milestones launch fireworks over the terminal. A failure resets the streak.

plugins.name: System monitor HUD
plugins.description: A heads-up display over your terminal: per-core CPU bars, memory and swap gauges, network throughput sparklines, load and the hungriest processes, refreshed every second.

plugins.name: Tab switcher
plugins.description: Find and focus kitty tabs by title with a native chooser.

plugins.name: Typing test
plugins.description: How fast do you really type code? A typing test made of real shell, Python, Rust and JavaScript lines, with live per-character feedback, WPM, accuracy and a personal best.

plugins.name: Warp screensaver
plugins.description: Leave kitty idle and it jumps to hyperspace: a starfield streaks out from the center of the screen over your terminal. Touch anything and you drop back to normal space.

plugins.name: Git worktree switcher
plugins.description: Choose a Git worktree and open it in a new kitty tab.
